turns.question: Where can I buy Thorne Basic Nutrients 2/Day at the best price from a reputable US retailer?
turns.shown:
**Short answer:** Almost every reputable US retailer lists the 60-capsule bottle at $36.00, so the price is nearly the same wherever you buy it. The lowest verified price is about $32 to $34 per 60 capsules, using a subscription discount or the larger bottle. Prices change often, so confirm the final price at checkout.

**What I found (listings checked today, but cached snippets can be stale):**
- **Standard 60-capsule bottle, $36.00:**
  - iHerb lists it at $36.00 [1].
  - Vitacost lists it at $36.00 [2] and Walmart.com lists it at $36.00 [3].
  - Swanson Vitamins lists it at $36.00 [4].
  - A clinic store shows it marked down from $38.99 to $36.00 [5].
- **Higher at local-delivery grocers:** PCC Community Markets lists it at $40.99 [6] and Mother's Market at $43.39 [7]. These are delivery-app prices and probably include markups.
- **120-capsule bottle, $68.00:** Vitacost lists it at $68.00 [8]. That works out to about $34 per 60 capsules, so it's slightly cheaper per capsule.
- **Subscription discounts:**
  - Thorne's own site says you save 10% when subscribed to 1–2 supplements, and 20% with 3 or more [9]. Subscription orders get free ground shipping within the contiguous US. [9] By my math, 10% off $36 is about $32.40, assuming Thorne's own price is also $36. I didn't see Thorne's product page price directly.
  - Amazon's Subscribe & Save page showed $30.60 with 15% savings [10]. That 15% applies only if you receive 5 or more products in one auto-delivery [10]. Otherwise the page says you'll save 10% [10], which is about $32.40. That page was flagged as old (about 469 days), so check it live.
- **Be careful with:** Price-comparison sites show lower numbers, for example $27.90 at Amazon as of September 2026 [11]. I couldn't confirm that on a current seller page, so don't count on it.

**Check the version.** Two versions exist. The "NSF Certified for Sport" 60-capsule version is $40.00 at iHerb [12]. The standard bottle is $36. Only pay more for the Sport version if you need that certification, for example for tested athletics.

**My judgment:** If you're happy to subscribe, the best deal is probably Thorne direct or Amazon Subscribe & Save, at roughly $31 to $32.40 per bottle. Both are cancelable. For a one-time purchase, $36 is the going price, and iHerb or Vitacost are fine. Vitacost says it sources products directly from brands or authorized distributors [13]. On Amazon, check that the seller is Amazon or Thorne. The listing I saw said "Sold by Pattern." [10] I couldn't confirm whether Pattern is an authorized Thorne seller.

**Before you buy:** Confirm the final price and the Sport vs. standard version. Check the "best by" date as well. Vitacost's page showed Best by 10/01/2027 [13].
